notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (all G1-G9 pass with no findings or warnings; evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). No hardware was attached, the hardware backend was never opened, and no hardware run is claimed. The upstream clone is one Python script of module-level functions (PowerSupply_Automation.py:99-130), not a class; it opens three VISA resources and a Modbus client at import (lines 49-57). This package does not import or run it. It is a ScpiDriver command map for the first supply, DCsupply_1 (line 11), and the two channels the upstream maps to it: channel 2 for S1 and channel 3 for S2 (lines 60-66). native names the card's Set_Voltage entry function for traceability only; the SCPI bridge opens the transport itself. Covered: voltage and current set points and output ON/OFF for channels 2 and 3 (the upstream commands INST:NSEL, VOLT, CURR, OUTP, lines 99-130); measured voltage and current through the upstream MEAS:VOLT? and MEAS:CURR? queries (lines 111-120); readback of the set points and output state through the standard query forms VOLT?, CURR? and OUTP? so every write has an observable state. The upstream never reads those set points or the output state back; the query suffixes are added for readback and the upstream write syntax is unchanged. NOT COVERED: DCsupply_2 and DCsupply_3, the S3-S5 channels, and the Modbus Watlow F4 temperature path (PowerSupply_Automation.py:133-141). One ScpiDriver transport opens one VISA resource, and the temperature controller is Modbus, not SCPI. The upstream has no simulator or tests, so fake.py is an in-memory transport with the write/read/query/close shape of the bridge, not a recording; every starting value and reading in it is marked '# placeholder'. Limits: the clone states no output voltage or current range; DEFAULT_VOLTAGE = 13.6 V and DEFAULT_CURRENT_LIMIT = 0.1 A are only the starting values of initialize_supplies, which the comment says can be changed (PowerSupply_Automation.py:26-28). The four numeric set points are therefore Limit.operator_required and are refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the operator supplies the installed unit's range in site-limits.json. site-limits.example.json is a deliberately narrow bench example (0 to 5 V and 0 to 0.05 A) and is not a statement about any installed unit; the gate's conformance run serves it so the operator-required paths are exercised. Safety: the supply can energize an external load, so the device is R2. The native stop and the safe_state=True action x-cap.madhankumar623.output_off.v1 send INST:NSEL 2;OUTP OFF;INST:NSEL 3;OUTP OFF, which switches both controlled channels off, the same operation the upstream shutdown_supplies loop performs for every mapped channel (lines 242-249). No line of the clone documents an independent hardware e-stop, so estop_physical_ref is not set and no hardware stop is claimed; the software latch and the safe-state action are not a safety-rated channel. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null): because it is R2, the loader refuses its hardware backend until a human sets reviewed_by. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; gate.digest is the digest the passing check printed.
